🪔 Diwali picks for 2026: 
Instead of 10-15, I have come out with "20 Small & Midcap Stocks From Leading Brokerages Worth Tracking"

As I mentioned that I was going through Diwali stock recommendations from leading brokerage houses & after reviewing recommendations from over 20 brokerages, including Motilal Oswal, JM Financial, Mirae Asset Sharekhan, SBI Securities, Arihant Capital, Monarch, Choice International and Equirus, I have narrowed down my initial list.

Most of the frequently recommended companies were largecaps. Nothing wrong with them, but my interest has always been more towards smaller businesses where earnings can grow much faster than the broader market. Particularly those where a 20–30% annual earnings growth, combined with reasonable valuations, can lead to disproportionate returns over 3–4 years.
For this exercise, I have kept the market capitalisation between ₹5,000 crore and ₹50,000 crore.
Here are the 20 names that made my initial shortlist.

20 Small & Midcap Stocks

1. Navin Fluorine (Mirae Asset Sharekhan, Shriram)

MCap: ~₹42,400 Cr

Specialty fluorochemicals and CDMO business. New capacities and higher-value products could improve profitability considerably. The growth opportunity is attractive, although much of the optimism is already reflected in valuations.

2. Blue Star (Monarch, Choice International)

MCap: ~₹32,500 Cr

India's room AC penetration remains relatively low. Blue Star has a strong position in cooling and commercial refrigeration. Capacity expansion and a growing distribution network could support earnings for several years.

3. Syrma SGS Technology (PL Capital)

MCap: ~₹28,100 Cr

Electronics manufacturing with exposure to industrial, automotive and consumer segments. Revenue growth is encouraging, but the more interesting opportunity lies in improving operating margins as the business scales.

4. Sansera Engineering (KC Securities)

MCap: ~₹25,700 Cr

Known for precision automotive components, but the expansion into aerospace, defence and other non-auto businesses could change its earnings profile over time. A business worth watching beyond the automobile cycle.

5. HBL Engineering (PL Capital)

MCap: ~₹23,300 Cr

One of the interesting companies in railway safety systems, particularly Kavach. The opportunity is sizeable, but orders need to translate into actual earnings and cash. The valuation also leaves limited room for disappointment.

6. Jyoti CNC Automation (SBI Securities)

MCap: ~₹23,200 Cr

India's growing investment in manufacturing and precision engineering works in its favour. SBI Securities expects around 34% PAT CAGR during FY26–FY28. A strong growth assumption, so execution will matter more than the narrative.

7. Lumax Auto Technologies (Mirae Asset Sharekhan, Choice International)

MCap: ~₹15,900 Cr

Increasing component content per vehicle, premiumisation and acquisitions are changing the scale of this business. If acquired businesses integrate well and margins improve, earnings could grow faster than revenue.

8. Shaily Engineering Plastics (Motilal Oswal)

MCap: ~₹14,000 Cr

Moving deeper into pharmaceutical drug delivery devices, particularly injection pens. Motilal Oswal expects around 48% annual PAT growth through FY28. The key question is how quickly the new customer programmes scale and how much is already priced in.

9. CCL Products (Monarch)

MCap: ~₹12,900 Cr

An established instant coffee exporter with a growing branded business. Higher capacity utilisation and expansion into value-added products could lift profitability. Coffee prices and operating margins remain important variables.

10. Ingersoll-Rand India (Choice International)

MCap: ~₹12,500 Cr

A high-quality industrial compressor business with a strong profitability record. Manufacturing capex and demand for energy-efficient equipment support growth. The attraction here is business quality, although the stock is rarely available at a bargain valuation.

11. VA Tech Wabag (Mirae Asset Sharekhan, Monarch)

MCap: ~₹12,400 Cr

Water treatment and desalination remain important investment areas. Wabag has an established position in both. The bigger question is how efficiently the company executes projects and converts its order book into cash.

12. Gravita India (JM Financial)

MCap: ~₹10,900 Cr

Recycling is becoming a more organised industry, and Gravita has been expanding across materials and geographies. New capacities and better utilisation could support earnings. Cash flows and returns on fresh investments will be worth tracking.

13. Unimech Aerospace (Motilal Oswal)

MCap: ~₹8,900 Cr

Precision manufacturing for aerospace and specialised engineering. Motilal Oswal projects 75% revenue and 69% PAT CAGR during FY26–FY28. These are exceptional growth expectations, but such numbers also leave little room for execution delays.

14. RateGain Travel Technologies (Choice International)

MCap: ~₹8,600 Cr

An interesting software business serving hotels, airlines and travel companies globally. Recurring revenues and operating leverage could improve profitability. The recent correction makes it worth revisiting, provided earnings expectations remain intact.

15. Time Technoplast (Equirus)

MCap: ~₹8,400 Cr

Industrial packaging may not sound particularly exciting, but the company's move towards composite cylinders and other higher-value products could improve margins and return ratios. An interesting business mix story.

16. Genus Power (SBI Securities)

MCap: ~₹8,000 Cr

One of the direct beneficiaries of India's smart meter rollout. The opportunity is large, but the real test is how quickly orders convert into revenue and, more importantly, cash. Working capital deserves particular attention.

17. Kirloskar Pneumatic (Arihant Capital)

MCap: ~₹7,400 Cr

An established industrial engineering business in compressors and refrigeration. Demand from manufacturing, process industries and industrial investment could support growth without depending on a single end market.

18. Technocraft Industries (Equirus)

MCap: ~₹6,200 Cr

A relatively less-discussed manufacturing company with industrial products, precision engineering and textiles. The interesting part is whether the growing higher-value engineering businesses can improve overall margins and profitability.

19. HEG Advanced Materials (Arihant Capital)

MCap: ~₹5,700 Cr

Battery materials, advanced carbon technologies and energy storage make this an interesting long-term opportunity. The ambitions are sizeable, but much of the new business is still being built. Execution over the next few years will determine how much value is actually created.

20. TD Power Systems (PL Capital)

MCap: ~₹18,600 Cr

Industrial generators with exposure to global power and infrastructure investments. Demand from exports and power equipment offers opportunities. Following the recent correction, the important question is whether earnings growth can justify the valuation.

Concluding Remarks:

What I found interesting is how strongly engineering, precision manufacturing, electronics and industrial businesses feature across these brokerage recommendations. A few companies have the potential to grow earnings at 25–30% annually, perhaps even higher. Some may also offer asymmetric opportunities if new capacities, better margins or business diversification deliver more than what the market currently expects.

But valuations cannot be ignored, specially in some of the momentum picks here.
I would rather buy a company growing earnings at 20–25% at a reasonable to very slightly expensive valuation than pay very excessive price for 35–40% growth.

My next step is to narrow these 20 names further, looking at FY27–FY30 earnings, ROCE, cash flows, debt and, most importantly, what is already priced into the stock. I will share the final shortlist, along with my detailed analysis and preferred picks, with WealthEnrich subscribers.
For now, these are research candidates drawn from brokerage recommendations, not a final buy list.

#HFCL and #STLTECH investors need to pay attention to what's happening in the US.

Goldman Sachs estimates that nearly 45% of planned US data-center capacity is in states that could face construction restrictions following the Democrats' election victories.

That is a significant number for companies benefiting from the AI infrastructure boom. But does it mean data-center demand is slowing, or are projects simply facing delays?

The 45% figure does not mean that 45% of data centers are being cancelled or that construction has already stopped. It represents planned capacity in states where new restrictions could potentially be introduced. Texas alone accounts for roughly 25% of planned US capacity.

The bigger question is why these restrictions are being discussed.

Data centers require enormous amounts of electricity, water and land. Many local communities are concerned that rapid construction could increase household electricity bills, strain power grids and consume resources that residents also depend on.

In Texas, newly elected Democratic Governor Gina Hinojosa has proposed temporarily stopping new data-center approvals until laws protecting local communities are introduced. These would address electricity costs, water consumption and the ability of residents to participate in decisions about developments near them.

Interestingly, this concern is not limited to Democrats. Outgoing Republican Governor Greg Abbott had already ordered a halt to certain data-center permits and grid connections while authorities examined their impact on electricity and water supplies.

Meanwhile, Donald Trump has reaffirmed his support for AI infrastructure. In his November 6 Truth Social statements, he said he would work with US states willing to welcome these investments.

So the situation is more complicated than Democrats opposing AI while Republicans support it. The disagreement is increasingly about how quickly data centers should be constructed, what safeguards should apply and who should bear the infrastructure costs.

There are also important implications for businesses supplying this infrastructure.

If a data-center project is delayed for six months, orders for GPUs, optical fibre, transformers, cooling systems and other equipment could also be pushed back. Suppliers expecting revenue from those projects may have to wait longer, affecting their quarterly growth and cash flows.

But delayed construction does not automatically mean demand has disappeared. Projects could eventually receive approvals or shift to other locations. The more serious problem would be projects getting permanently cancelled because of higher costs or stricter regulations.

For HFCL and Sterlite, which are expanding their exposure to AI and optical connectivity infrastructure, this makes customer order schedules and actual deliveries particularly important.

Sterlite has announced a multi-year product award worth more than $1 billion for optical connectivity products supporting US AI data centers. HFCL has reported an order book exceeding ₹28,900 crore, supported by demand across optical fibre, telecom networks and data-center connectivity.

However, neither company's total order book should be treated as entirely dependent on US data-center construction, and the 45% estimate cannot directly be converted into a revenue impact for either business.

There is another important data point from Goldman Sachs. In October, before these election results, it maintained that US data-center growth through 2027 remained broadly intact, forecasting total capacity of 64 GW by the end of 2026 and 90 GW by the end of 2027.

The new political developments create additional uncertainty around those expectations. Goldman has since indicated that it expects potential construction moratoriums to be relatively short-lived, although that is still a forecast.

Supriya Lifescience Ltd.

Q2FY27 result
While the topline crossed the ₹200 crore quarterly mark, operating margins experienced a sharp reality check.

Revenue: ₹206.3 Cr (+3.2% YoY, +8.7% QoQ) | H1 Revenue: ₹396.0 Cr (+14.8% YoY)
EBITDA: ₹45.4 Cr (-37.5% YoY) | EBITDA Margin: 22.0% (vs 36.4% in Q2 FY26 & 25.0% in Q1 FY27)
PAT: ₹29.3 Cr (-42.0% YoY, +21.7% QoQ) | PAT Margin: 14.2%
Balance Sheet: Zero debt with ~₹182.5 Cr in liquid cash/investment

After guiding for a structural 33–35% margin corridor in August, management was transparent in attributing the margin contraction to three simultaneous headwinds

Regulatory Shifts in LATAM
Policy changes slowed dispatches of high margin products to LATAM (revenue mix dropped from 21% to 12%), forcing a temporary shift in volumes toward lower margin, semi regulated markets.

Ambernath Facility Drag
The newly commissioned finished dosage (FDF) plant is in its active ramp up phase. Fixed overheads, quality team expansion, and trial runs are hitting the P&L ahead of commercial revenue scale.

Persistent Solvent & Input Inflation
Geopolitical conflicts and freight disruptions kept raw material and solvent costs elevated, pulling gross margins down ~650 bps YoY to 65.6%.

Despite near term margin volatility, Supriya achieved major strategic milestones during the quarter

Commercial Formulation Debut
Successfully commercialised and launched two new liquid inhalation anesthetic formulations from the Ambernath site, with an initial exhibit batch order bagged for RoW markets.

Semaglutide / GLP-1 Breakthrough
Developed and filed a patent for a novel oral Semaglutide tablet formulation, and is actively collaborating with a leading Indian generics major for GLP-1 portfolio development and supply.

Regulated Market Inroads
Europe surged to 43% of total revenues (vs 37% last year), while North America expanded to 5% as validation batches for its 22 US DMF filings gained traction.

Working Capital Discipline
Trade receivables were aggressively collected, dropping from ₹219 Cr in March to ₹126 Cr in September releasing nearly ₹94 Cr of cash back into the business.

Topline Goal
 Management’s stated target of ₹1,000 Cr for FY27 implies delivering ₹604 Cr in H2 (~₹302 Cr per quarter). While H2 is seasonally stronger, reaching ₹1,000 Cr without large, lumpy CDMO licensing dispatches will be a steep climb.

Operating Leverage
 Ambernath’s opex drag will only reverse once commercial volumes ramp and unit costs are absorbed across its five operational FDF lines.

Triggers to Track Over the Next 60 Days

The November 2026 EU-GMP Audit at the Ambernath formulations site the critical regulatory passport for European CMO/CDMO contracts.

Execution of the Anesthetic CDMO Contract, where management previously indicated they were close to finalizing a major term sheet.

Margin Recovery Trajectory Pace of customer price pass throughs in H2.

📰 今日 SpaceX 投资早报｜2026.11.07

Baron 之夜把 SpaceX 的全貌摊开了

每日一报跟踪Elon 生态全景：SpaceX / xAI / AI / Tesla。我是 Kiko，一个长期拿 SpaceX 的人，用持有者的眼睛抓新闻。

🚀 SpaceX

📡 范登堡又一发 27 颗星链入轨，一级 B1093 第 18 飞，41 天周转即复飞。

📊 这是 SpaceX 今年第 122 发——与全世界其他国家加起来打平，122:122。入轨流水线这个词，早就不是比喻了。

🛰️ Starship Flight 15 目标 11 月 13 日：B22＋Ship 42，第一次同任务双捕——超重助推器和飞船都由发射塔机械臂接住。SpaceX 发射副总裁 Dontchev 11 月 5 日在 UP.Summit 亲口给的日期；Musk 在 Baron 大会上说，大约一周后就试。FAA 执照还没下来，这是目前唯一的卡点。昨天 SpaceX 还放出了纪录片《Go For Orbit》，讲的就是这次任务背后的故事。

🌌 北京时间今早 8:48，范登堡排期一发涉密任务 USSF-432，B1095 第 8 飞。

🛰️ StarMind 来了：Musk 在 Baron 大会上说，SpaceX 与 NVIDIA 联合设计的 StarMind 天基 AI 计算机，2027 年第三季度开始发射，2028 年放量、2029 年再上一个量级，星座规划可达 100 万颗 AI 卫星。他的原话：太空里算力的成本，一旦每吨入轨成本降下来，会比地面便宜得多。

📶 星链 V3 同样在加速：单星能力是 V2 的 10 倍以上，发射数量也是 10 倍，2–3 年内星链总带宽提升约 100 倍，V4 还在后面。

🧠 xAI / Grok / Grok Bot

🏢 11 月 6 日，印度 IT 公司 Coforge 加入 SpaceX 超级智能合作伙伴网络（SpaceXSI），成为 Transformation Partner——用 Grok 的产品组合（聊天、推理、开发、企业自动化、语音、图像视频）进企业生产环境。这是 Grok 从消费者产品走向企业订单的一步。

🧠 Grok 5 还在训：Colossus 2 集群，11 万块 GB200＋44 万块 GB300，当前公开模型仍是 Grok 4.7。

💰 Musk 在 Baron 大会上给的数字：SpaceX（含 xAI）年化收入 2026 年 12 月将超 1000 亿美元，2027 年 12 月或超 5000 亿美元，1 万亿也不是没可能、概率约 2%。他自己补了一句：这不是承诺，是 best guess。

🤖 AI

① SpaceX: $500B Revenue Run Rate by 2027?

At the Ron Baron conference, Musk projected annualized revenue exceeding $100B by December 2026 and potentially $500B by December 2027. He put the odds of $1T at just 2%.

Ambitious forecasts, not actual revenue. Cash flow remains the ultimate test.

② Tesla to End Cybertruck Production

Musk plans to phase out Cybertruck production by mid-2027, shifting capacity toward Cybercab.

2025 U.S. sales: 20,237, down 48% YoY.

The question: Can Robotaxi deployment absorb Cybercab production?

③ StarMind: Orbital AI Launches in 2027

SpaceX and NVIDIA aim to launch their first StarMind AI computers in Q3 2027, scaling through 2029.

The vision is ambitious. Cooling, maintenance, and economics remain unproven.

④ Starship Tower Catch Coming Soon

Musk says SpaceX could attempt its first Starship upper-stage tower catch in about a week, potentially using Ship 42.

A major reusability milestone if successful. Timing remains tentative.

⑤ Tesla’s Terafab Takes Shape

Tesla is building a semiconductor research facility at Giga Texas, supporting its proposed Grimes County Terafab.

Musk’s long-term target: 1 TW of annual AI chip capacity.

Scaling advanced chip manufacturing remains a formidable challenge.

⑥ Starlink Targets 100x Bandwidth Growth

Musk expects network bandwidth to increase roughly 100-fold within 2–3 years.

He also raised the possibility of acquiring a telecom operator for spectrum. No deal announced.

⑦ Optimus: Leasing Over Selling?

Musk favors a potential leasing model for Optimus, creating recurring revenue.

But production-scale reliability and unit economics remain unproven.

⑧ Grok Expands Into Enterprise AI

India’s Coforge joins the SpaceX Super Intelligence Partner Network to integrate Grok into enterprise workflows.

A new distribution channel beyond consumer subscriptions.

⑨ Russia Wants Its Own Starlink

Russia is accelerating domestic satellite internet development, citing security concerns over foreign networks.

Satellite connectivity is increasingly strategic infrastructure.

① Musk：SpaceX明年12月年化收入可能超过5,000亿美元

在11月6日Ron Baron投资会议上，Musk表示：2026年12月年化收入有望超过1,000亿美元。2027年12月年化收入很可能超过5,000亿美元。1万亿美元并非完全不可能，但他自己估计概率仅约2%。

这些都是Musk的预测，并非已实现收入或正式业绩指引。尤其要注意，年末年化收入不等于全年实际收入。如此激进的增长目标，关键取决于AI算力需求、交付能力和现金流兑现。

② Tesla宣布2027年中逐步停止Cybertruck生产

Musk确认Tesla计划于2027年中前后逐步停止德州工厂的Cybertruck生产，将产能转向Cybercab。

Cybertruck在美国2025年销量为20,237辆，较2024年下降48%，远低于最初每年25万辆的目标。

③ StarMind太空AI计算机：计划2027年第三季度首次发射

Musk表示，SpaceX与NVIDIA共同设计的StarMind计算机可能于2027年第三季度开始进入轨道，2028年扩大部署，2029年进一步加速。

他认为低发射成本与太空太阳能最终可能降低AI计算成本。但这仍是工程和经济模型上的预测，尚未证明大规模轨道计算的散热、维护和商业回报。

④ Starship：Musk称约一周后尝试首次飞船塔架捕获

Musk表示，SpaceX准备在约一周后尝试用发射塔机械臂捕获返回的Starship上面级，预计涉及Ship 42。

这是公司计划中的测试，并非已确认的发射许可或最终日期。如果成功，将是Starship全面复用的重要里程碑。

⑤ Terafab：Tesla德州研究晶圆厂进入建设阶段

Musk表示，Tesla正在Giga Texas建设研究型晶圆制造设施，用于测试新工艺，未来再向Grimes County规划的大型Terafab转移。

他提出长期年产1太瓦AI芯片的目标，并承认项目规模巨大、失败风险很高。

研究设施与商业规模先进制程量产之间仍有巨大距离，良率、资本开支及外部晶圆厂合作将决定项目进展。

⑥ Starlink：Musk预计未来两三年网络带宽提升约100倍

Musk称第三代Starlink卫星单星能力较上一代提升十倍以上，随着部署扩大，整体网络带宽有望大幅增长。

他还提出未来可能收购传统电信运营商，以获得更多频谱，但没有宣布具体收购目标。

⑦ Optimus：Musk倾向机器人租赁商业模式

在Ron Baron访谈中，Musk认为成熟人形机器人有机会实现远高于人类的持续工作产出，并表示租赁可能是Optimus更合适的商业模式。

这可能带来持续性收入，但目前没有量产规模的生产率、故障率或单位经济数据支持其长期估算。

⑧ Grok企业市场：印度Coforge加入SpaceXSI合作伙伴网络

11月6日，印度IT服务商Coforge宣布加入SpaceX Super Intelligence Partner Network，作为Transformation Partner，帮助企业将Grok应用于软件现代化、客服和业务流程。

财务条款未披露。Grok正尝试通过系统集成商进入企业工作流程，而不只是依靠消费者订阅。

Everybody's talking about how powerful AI is getting. I'm looking at who's going to control it—and who makes the money.

NVIDIA is reportedly pushing TSMC to explore next-generation memory chips while helping expand advanced chip-packaging capacity.

Elon Musk's Grok is moving deeper into corporate America through a new partnership with Coforge.

Meanwhile, a smaller developer called Underdog is demonstrating an AI voice model small enough to run locally, without relying on massive cloud servers.

Now hold on. Look at what's happening.

NVIDIA is working to secure the hardware. Grok is pursuing business customers. Smaller AI developers are trying to make some of that expensive infrastructure unnecessary.

Three different strategies. Billions of dollars potentially at stake.

My take: The next AI race isn't just about who builds the smartest model. It's about who controls the chips, who wins the customers, and who can deliver useful AI at the lowest cost.

And with a new Congress coming in, questions about regulation, China, energy costs and corporate financing aren't going away.

Bottom line: America needs to stay competitive. But before celebrating every billion-dollar AI announcement, I'd like to see something simple.

Who's paying? Who's profiting? And does the technology actually work?

Nifty suddenly out of the blues, reclaiming the 25,000 mark on 6 November 2026 after months below it, while AI/data-centre-heavy portfolios have moved in the opposite direction and value + steady-growth oriented ones have shown clear relative strength.

Drivers included heavy FII buying (very large single-day inflows earlier in the week), strength in banking/financials and select large-caps, better-than-expected corporate earnings in parts of the market, and India decoupling from a sharp global tech/AI-linked sell-off on Wall Street.

Broader mid/small-cap indices lagged the benchmarks. AI / Data-Centre (AI DC) heavy portfolios going the other way.

👉India’s listed “AI enabler” or data-centre supply-chain names (optical fibre, power equipment, cooling, transformers, gensets, related industrials, etc.) had been standout performers earlier in 2026 even while the broader Nifty lagged. 

👉Names linked to hyperscaler/data-centre capex (examples that had run hard include Sterlite Technologies, HFCL, MTAR, TD Power Systems and various power/electrical equipment plays) delivered large gains as investors chased the global AI infrastructure theme.

Trigger was the broader Wall Street tech sell-off (linked in part to political/regulatory worries around data-centre expansion and AI spending after US midterms), profit-taking after huge earlier runs, and stretched valuations in the Indian AI-proxy basket. 

👉Portfolios heavily concentrated in these AI/data-centre beneficiaries underperformed (or declined) even as the Nifty recovered strongly.

👉Value + steady-growth stocks showing relative strength

The recovery was led by more traditional, higher-quality, less thematic names...particularly private banks and financials (HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis, etc.), plus select large-cap earners with steadier growth profiles (e.g., Mahindra & Mahindra stood out on earnings). These areas provided the bulk of the index lift.​

Portfolios built around value characteristics (reasonable valuations, earnings visibility, balance-sheet strength) plus consistent compounders therefore held up better or gained relative to the pure AI DC cohort. 

👉This fits a classic rotation pattern: when a high-momentum thematic trade gets crowded and then hits profit-taking/valuation pressure (especially if global catalysts turn), capital tends to rotate toward steadier domestic growth and value-oriented large-caps that benefit from local flows, earnings, and lower beta to global tech sentiment.

 The AI/data-centre trade that had been one of the few bright spots in a tough 2026 for Indian equities is currently experiencing the classic “what goes up a lot can correct hard” phase, while more traditional value-plus-steady-growth constructions are outperforming on a relative basis.

Happy Forgings: भट्टी, हथौड़ा, और 30% margin

Ludhiana की Happy Forgings गर्म steel को भारी presses से ठोककर engine के सबसे कठिन हिस्से बनाती है: crankshafts, जो truck, tractor और industrial engines का दिल हैं। फिर उन्हें machine करके तैयार part देती है।

Jul-Sep 2026:
Revenue ₹501 cr, साल भर पहले ₹377 cr (+33%)
Operating profit ₹153 cr, margin 30.5%
Net profit ₹98 cr, Apr-Jun के ₹91 cr से +8%

₹100 का हिसाब: ₹69.5 steel, बिजली, लोग और बाक़ी खर्च में गए, ₹11 interest-depreciation-tax में, और ₹19.6 net profit बना।

Forging में 30% margin असाधारण क्यों है? आम forging company 15-20% पर काम करती है। Happy Forgings का फ़र्क़ तीन चीज़ों में है: (1) बहुत भारी parts, जिनके लिए बड़ी press चाहिए जो कम companies के पास है; (2) machining in-house, यानी value add ज़्यादा; (3) exports और industrial (non-auto) ग्राहक, जो quality के लिए कीमत देते हैं।

पर इस quarter margin 31.4% से 30.5% पर आया, और incremental margin ~23% रहा, औसत से कम। Management पहले ही कह चुका है कि वो margin FY26 के स्तर पर स्थिर रखने का लक्ष्य रखता है, growth volume से। यानी इस margin को और ऊपर जाने की उम्मीद नहीं, स्थिर रहने की।

Cycle का ध्यान: truck और tractor की बिक्री चक्र में चलती है। जब धीमी होती है, forging company के plant खाली रहते हैं और fixed खर्च margin को दबाता है।

सबक: ऊँचा margin अक्सर एक "कठिन काम" से आता है जिसे दूसरे आसानी से नहीं कर सकते। उस कठिनाई को पहचानिए, वही moat है।

Supriya Lifescience, Q2 FY27 — a weak quarter, and management has cut its margin guidance.

Revenue ₹206.3 Cr, +3.2% YoY (+8.7% QoQ). 
EBITDA ₹45.4 Cr, −37.5% YoY, margin 22.0% vs 36.4%. PAT ₹29.3 Cr, −42% YoY, margin 14.2%. 
H1: revenue ₹396 Cr (+14.8%), EBITDA ₹93 Cr (−25.3%, 23.4% margin), PAT ₹53 Cr (−37.5%).

What management said on the call: 
→ Normal margin is 34–35%; Q2 is 11–12 points below that. Roughly 6 points from the Ambernath plant (~₹60 Cr of FY27 costs, almost no revenue this year because the EU audit slipped), ~3 from LATAM and ~3 from raw material and solvent prices 
→ LATAM: several countries reclassified high-margin products as controlled substances with immediate effect. Customers need import permits, which take 4–5 months. LATAM fell to 12% of sales from 21%. Management calls it deferral, not lost demand 
→ Raw material price increases reach large contract customers with a lag, so the benefit shows in 2–3 quarters 
→ FY27 EBITDA margin guidance cut to 23–25% (~25% for the rest of the year). No FY28 margin guidance yet 
→ ₹1,000 Cr FY27 revenue target kept. H1 is ₹396 Cr, so H2 needs ~₹604 Cr → 20%+ annual revenue growth guided for the next 3–4 years

Pipeline: two anaesthetic liquid inhalation products launched, two ADHD products coming, contrast media next quarter, and a large CDMO contract described as close. New launches are selling mainly in lower-price semi-regulated markets for now.

Balance sheet: no borrowings, but inventory is ₹265 Cr vs ₹160 Cr in March.

Ambernath EU audit starts next week. Q3 and Q4 are expected to be at a low margin level.

• Transformation Partners, Not System Integrators: Traditional IT integrators just maintain old infrastructure. Grok "Transformation Partners" are deploying full-stack AI swarms that rewrite internal software pipelines while existing systems are still running.

• The Enterprise Monetization Shift: This marks xAI’s direct push to capture enterprise market share from OpenAI and Anthropic by leveraging global IT service networks to handle the heavy integration lift.

The old IT playbook of billing clients per human hour to write basic enterprise code is officially dead.

India ignored a global tech wipeout today and closed up 2%. The more useful thing happened underneath.

The market split the AI trade into victims and beneficiaries for the first time, and it did it on a day the index was up.

IT services got the bid, on a clean argument. If clients stop pouring money into data centres, the money comes back to ordinary outsourcing. Nifty IT opened up 2.35% on that thesis. It closed up 0.43%. Mphasis ran 8% intraday, Infosys and TCS up to 3%, and the whole leg was sold into through the afternoon.

Meanwhile India's actual AI capex supply chain was taken apart. TD Power Systems fell 13.5%, Apar Industries 9.4%, Netweb 6.1%, with CG Power, MTAR, Hitachi Energy, HFCL and Sterlite Tech down up to 15%. Thermax added a miss of its own, falling about 17% on profit down 5% and order booking down 8%, and now sits 46% below its June high.

That is the real information. This complex has been re-rated on an India transmission capex story for two years, with global data centre demand quietly doing part of the work in the multiple. Today the market priced that second leg separately and marked it down. Anyone holding it on a grid capex thesis now has to say how much of the multiple was actually an AI datacentre multiple. Nobody discloses that, because order inflows there are reported as one number.

The tape. Nifty closed 25,030.35, up 2.01%. Sensex up 1,718 points. Seventh straight up session, best week in six years, Nifty up 8.6%. Bank Nifty hit an eight month high. Banks did all of it.

And breadth was negative. On the NSE, 1,439 stocks advanced against 2,141 declining. Midcap 100 flat, Smallcap 100 down 0.82%, India VIX up about 13% to 17.7 on a 2% up day. Ten heavyweights, not a market.

Flows explain the decoupling. Foreign investors bought a net 14,975 crore rupees on Thursday, the biggest single day in nearly six years, with domestics selling 10,445 crore into it. Five straight foreign buying sessions, roughly 35,800 crore, accelerating every day. Friday's number is not out yet, and that is the test.

Confused About IPO Shareholder Quota? Let's Understand When to Buy Shares! 📊

There are 4 major stages before an IPO reaches the RHP stage.

1️⃣ Company Has Not Filed DRHP
Avoid buying shares solely for shareholder quota at this stage.
Example: GAIL Gas IPO (only a possibility; DRHP not filed yet).

2️⃣ Company Files DRHP
If you are not regularly tracking SEBI approval updates, you may consider holding 1 share as an early watchlist position.
Examples:
• JSW Cement / JSW Steel
• Coal India / Southern Coalfields Ltd.

3️⃣ SEBI Approves DRHP
This is generally a more informed stage to evaluate buying shares for the shareholder quota.
Example: Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd. (subject to IPO timeline and eligibility conditions).

4️⃣ Company Files RHP
This is a crucial stage. Check the official record date, eligibility criteria and shareholding requirements before making any decision.

IMPORTANT:
Buying shares does not guarantee IPO allotment. Always verify the official RHP and record-date requirements.

Simple rule: Track DRHP → Monitor SEBI Approval → Check RHP → Verify Record Date.

Blockers
• Q1 PAT fell 14% against guided mid-teens PBT growth, and FY27 double-digit PBT growth is now uncertain.

Sudarshan Chemical Industries | Q2 FY27 results

Sudarshan's Q2 profit before tax more than doubles YoY despite ₹83 Cr exceptional charge

👉 Sudarshan Chemical Industries reported consolidated revenue from operations of ₹2,742.6 Cr for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, up 14.9% from ₹2,387.4 Cr a year earlier and 3.8% above Q1's ₹2,642.1 Cr. Profit before tax was ₹71.4 Cr, against ₹29.5 Cr a year ago, after an exceptional expense of ₹82.9 Cr. Net profit was ₹30.5 Cr, compared with ₹19.3 Cr a year ago and ₹103.4 Cr in Q1.

👉 Raw material cost grew faster than sales, reaching ₹1,449.1 Cr, up 18.9% on a year earlier. Employee costs were ₹436.3 Cr against ₹415.7 Cr, and other expenses climbed to ₹726.0 Cr from ₹648.7 Cr. Other income fell to ₹14.9 Cr from ₹28.8 Cr, reducing support to profit. Operating margin, as shown in the results table, slipped to 2.6% from 5.9% in Q1.

👉 Before the exceptional item, pre-tax profit was ₹154.3 Cr, close to Q1's ₹157.4 Cr and well above ₹29.5 Cr a year ago. Operating cash flow for the half-year was ₹286.4 Cr, against an outflow of ₹141.9 Cr in the same period last year. Management has guided the acquired Heubach group to about €700 Mn of FY27 sales and €35 Mn EBITDA, a target reaffirmed in August. The filing does not split out that group, so this quarter cannot be measured against that guidance from these numbers.

हिंदुओं की समस्या यह है कि उन्होंने अपने ग्रंथ नहीं पढे हैं, और वह 2014 के बाद ही हिंदू बने हैं। ना उन्होंने वेद दर्शन उपनिषद रामायण महाभारत पढे हैं। यहां तक की उन्होंने गीता भी नहीं पढी है।
लोग सोचते हैं कि रामायण पूरी तरह वाल्मीकि रामायण पर बनाई जानी चाहिए थी, पर सच कहूं तो हिंदू उसे झेल भी नहीं पाएगा, और डायरेक्टर प्रोड्यूसर को मारने से पहले खुद अपने नाखूनों से अपना सीना फाड़ लेगा।
कुछ लोग अभी बकवास कर रहे हैं कि माता सीता श्री राम को सीधे राम क्यों बोल रही हैं? मैंने कहा न यह लोग 2014 के बाद हिंदू बने हैं। और तब से केवल हिंदू नाम के कारण माइलेज ले रहे हैं। अच्छा वक्त बीता पिछले एक दशक में, बढ़िया होता एक दो धार्मिक पुस्तक पढ़ लेते तो आज उछल-उछल कर हिंदुत्व की बात न करनी पड़ती। पढ़ते रहे हैं रामचरितमानस और सब कुछ चाहिए वाल्मीकि रामायण के हिसाब से!

माता सीता एक दो बार नहीं बल्कि कई बार उनको राम और राघव कह कर बुलाती हैं। अब तुमको यह वोकिज्म लग रहा है। क्योंकि अब तुम हर चीज को अपने ग्रंथ के नहीं बल्कि ट्रोल्स और पश्चिम की नजर से देखने लगे हो। अब हम एक प्राइम हिन्दुत्व में जी रहे हैं जहाँ हम अपने धर्म ग्रंथ की भाषा आदि अपने-अपने पैमाने पर सेट करके ही मानेंगे। उसी से पता लगेगा कि सबसे बड़ा हिंदू कौन है।

कुछ लोग रामानंद सागर को ही वाल्मीकि समझकर कह रहे हैं कि क्योंकि रामानंद सागर ने माता सीता को कभी हाथ में अस्त्र-शस्त्र लेते हुए नहीं दिखाया इसलिए अब जो भी दिखाएगा वह हिंदुत्व विरोधी हो जाएगा। जबकि वह यह भूल जाते हैं की माता सीता एक क्षत्राणी थी और वह धनुर्विद्या तथा तलवार चलाने में महारथी थी। अगर वह भगवान शिव का पिनाक उठाकर रख सकती थी तो क्या वह तलवार नहीं चला सकती थी? लेकिन यहां भी लोगों को हॉलीवुड की नकल पहले दिखने लग जाती है अपने ग्रंथ नहीं।

फिर कुछ लोगों ने आपत्ति जताई कि क्योंकि रामानंद सागर ने तो विवाह स्थल पर ही परशुराम संवाद दिखाया था इसलिए जो यह नहीं दिखाएगा वह भी हिंदू विरोधी होगा जबकि वाल्मीकि रामायण में यह प्रकरण मिथिला में ही परंतु बारात वापसी के मार्ग में बताया गया है।

फिर कुछ लोगों को समस्या हुई की इसमें तो सूर्पनखा का नाक काटते समय फेमिनिज्म को बढ़ावा दिया गया है जबकि रामानंद सागर की रामायण में स्वयं राम लक्ष्मण से कहते हैं कि तुमने अच्छा नहीं किया।

फिर यह बात उठा दी गई कि रावण का महिमा मंडन किया जा रहा है, उसे रेपिस्ट नहीं दिखाया गया। जबकि रामानंद सागर ने स्वयं हनुमान जी से और श्री राम जी से रावण का महिमा मंडन करवाया था। किसी ने उसे रेपिस्ट नहीं दिखाया हालाँकि वो था। हर चीज दिखाई नहीं जाती, पढी सब जाती हैं। परंतु रामानंद सागर की रामायण देखते समय हमारी आंखों में आंसू आ जाते हैं और हम कहते हैं कि यह हमारा इतिहास है इस पर हमें गर्व है इसने वर्ल्ड रिकॉर्ड बना दिया।

यह किसी फिल्म का प्रमोशन नहीं बल्कि मैं इस पोस्ट के जरिए वाल्मीकि रामायण का प्रमोशन करना चाहता हूं। जितने में आप एक टिकट लेंगे उससे कम पैसे में एक वाल्मीकि रामायण आ जाएगी जो आपके घर में अगले 50 साल तक रहेगी और आपकी पीढ़ियां उसको पढेंगी। लेकिन समस्या यही है कि पढ़ना आसान नहीं होता और हिंदू के लिए तो बिल्कुल भी नहीं, पर फिर भी मैं कहूंगा...

Are Groww (Billionbrains Garage Ventures) and National Stock Exchange (NSE) Technology Companies? Absolutely! Both are technology-driven businesses, although their business models are different.

Groww and NSE represent India's rapidly expanding digital financial infrastructure. Groww, operated by Billionbrains Garage Ventures, is a fintech platform whose core business is built around technology, digital brokerage, mobile applications, cloud infrastructure, data analytics and seamless online investing. Its ability to scale customers without proportionately increasing physical infrastructure is its biggest strength.

Similarly, the National Stock Exchange (NSE) is fundamentally a technology-driven financial market institution. Its business depends on sophisticated trading engines, high-speed order matching, electronic trading platforms, risk-management algorithms, cybersecurity, data centres and massive transaction-processing capabilities.

Neither is a conventional IT services company like TCS or Infosys. However, technology is the backbone of their operations, scalability and competitive advantage.

My view: Both deserve recognition as technology-led financial businesses. India's digital financial revolution will create enormous long-term opportunities for such platforms.

Coforge has broken out to a fresh record high - and the fundamental momentum underneath is getting stronger.

Q2 FY27:

Revenue ₹6,171 Cr, +54% YoY
EBITDA ₹1,270 Cr, +67%
EBITDA margin 20.6%
PAT ₹588 Cr, +57%
But the bigger trigger is the deal pipeline.

Coforge signed 8 large deals in Q2 - the highest ever in a single quarter.

Order intake crossed $1.04 Bn, while the executable 12-month order book reached $2.38 Bn, +45% YoY.

Management believes even this large-deal record could be beaten in Q3.

The second trigger is AI.

AI-led Engineering + Data + Cloud already contribute ~86% of revenue, while Coforge is running 500+ AI engagements across 225 clients.

And today, Coforge joined SpaceX’s Super Intelligence Partner Network to help enterprises deploy Grok into production.

So AI is moving from: Pilot projects to Enterprise implementation + engineering + automation + large transformation deals.

The macro also helps as banks, insurers and governments modernise legacy systems and increase AI adoption.

Encora integration is running ahead of plan, while Coforge has raised FY27 EBIT margin guidance to 16% and targets ~17% in Q4.

Management’s longer-term aspiration is to reach ~$5 Bn revenue by FY30.

Key monitorable: whether record deal wins continue converting into strong organic growth while margins keep expanding.

Supriya Lifescience | Q2 FY27 results

Supriya Lifescience profit falls 42% to ₹29.2 Cr as margin drops to 18%

👉 Supriya Lifescience reported standalone revenue from operations of ₹206.3 Cr for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, up 3.3% from ₹199.8 Cr a year earlier and 8.8% from ₹189.7 Cr in the June quarter. Net profit fell 42.1% year on year to ₹29.2 Cr, from ₹50.4 Cr, while profit before tax fell 44.7% to ₹37.8 Cr. Other income was ₹2.3 Cr. Exceptional items were nil.

👉 Operating margin fell to 18.1% from 33.7% a year ago and 21.2% in the June quarter. Cost of materials was ₹92.5 Cr, or 44.8% of revenue, against 30.4% a year earlier and 57.7% in the June quarter. A ₹21.4 Cr rise in stock of finished goods and work-in-progress, against ₹53.0 Cr in Q1, lowered the cost line. Other expenditure rose 35.6% to ₹63.7 Cr and depreciation rose 42.5% to ₹9.5 Cr.

👉 Inventories rose 66% to ₹265.2 Cr from ₹159.6 Cr at March 31, absorbing ₹105.6 Cr of cash, while trade receivables fell to ₹125.6 Cr from ₹219.4 Cr, releasing ₹93.9 Cr. Operating cash flow for the half year was ₹60.9 Cr, against ₹137.5 Cr for all of FY26. Capital spending was ₹35.4 Cr. The company has no borrowings, and cash plus bank balances rose to ₹75.9 Cr from ₹37.5 Cr.

👉 Revenue grew 14.8% in the first half to ₹396.0 Cr, below the 20% annual growth management reaffirmed in June. Reaching the ₹1,000 Cr FY27 revenue target would need ₹604 Cr in the second half, about ₹302 Cr a quarter, against ₹206.3 Cr in Q2. Management had also guided to 33-35% EBITDA margins; the reported operating margin of 18.1% sits well below that range.

👉 Growth catalyst: Management targets ₹1,000 Cr revenue for FY27, is spending ₹200 Cr on Patalganga Phase 1, and plans a new dedicated manufacturing unit for finished dosage forms.

👉 Road blocker: Operating margin fell to 18.1% from 33.7% a year ago, well below the 33-35% EBITDA range management had guided to.

Happy Forgings | Record volumes, a larger capex plan, and a cash-conversion test

Happy Forgings crossed ₹500 crore of quarterly revenue in Q2 FY27. The more useful detail is how it got there: finished-goods volumes rose 24.8% YoY and EBITDA per kg increased to ₹82 from ₹77 a year earlier.

Revenue reached ₹501 crore, up 32.7%. EBITDA grew 32.2% to ₹153 crore and PAT rose 32.8% to ₹98 crore. Realisation increased 6.3%, helped by raw-material pass-through, negotiated conversion-cost recovery and product mix. The growth therefore has a substantial volume component, rather than relying entirely on higher selling prices.

The profit-per-kg improvement deserves attention because EBITDA margin slipped 11 basis points YoY and 76 basis points sequentially to 30.6%. Freight and other cost pressures are absorbing part of the benefit from stronger volumes and price resets. Investors should track both percentage margins and per-unit profitability.

The expansion announcement connects directly to that operating picture. The board approved another ₹500 crore of capex across FY28 and FY29. Management said roughly 70% will go into machining, with the remainder in small forging presses. H1 machining utilisation was 77%, against 60% for forging. Management expects machining utilisation to approach 90% by Q4, explaining why value-added capacity is getting priority.

This new programme is separate from the existing ₹650 crore heavy-component expansion. The latest call adds an important clarification: management described secured data-centre-related orders as approximately ₹300 crore per annum, with a contract running to 2033. That is management's stated annual business visibility, not current revenue or a guarantee of full utilisation.

The conversion timetable still matters. Cold trials are planned for January–February, hot trials for March, followed by sampling. Heavy-component revenue is expected from Q3/Q4 FY28. The August call already set that revenue timetable and expected a meaningful contribution from FY29, so the latest wording should not be mistaken for a fresh revenue delay. Equally, the ₹500 crore order-closure objective for March remains a target, not an achieved order book.

Against previous commitments, execution is encouraging but incomplete. August's high-teen full-year volume-growth guidance is supported by 24% H1 growth. The above-30% margin ambition is holding. However, OEM price revisions have not prevented sequential margin compression, and the solar-power savings remain ahead rather than in reported earnings.

Cash conversion is the main counterweight. H1 operating cash flow fell to about ₹124 crore from ₹217 crore a year earlier, while PAT rose 35.8%. Management cited receivables growth and ₹35 crore of supplier advances and expects normalisation. Gross borrowings and lease liabilities also rose to approximately ₹543 crore from ₹330 crore at March-end. With capex increasing, that cash-flow recovery needs to show up in the accounts.

Kyro view: the current volume growth and improving EBITDA per kg make the execution case more credible. The next proof points are Q3 recognition of North American PV shipments, recovery in cash conversion, and heavy-line trials progressing into customer approvals. The longer-term opportunity is substantial, but the earnings contribution will arrive in stages.

Segment Trends
•CV (33% of H1 revenue): high-teen growth, domestic mid-20s in line with MHCV; exports subdued on longer shipments
•Farm equipment (30%): >20% growth; domestic outperformed tractor production; market share gains (now ~36% from 42% earlier base); no material impact expected from any OEM caution
•Industrial (16%): >50% growth; strong domestic + export; data-centre backup power and energy a key driver
•Construction equipment (12%): >50% growth
•Passenger vehicle (9%): nearly doubled; both domestic and export; dedicated North American PV line ramping (sales recognition from Q3; ~₹80–100 cr projected)

Capacity & CapEx
•Current: 1.58 lakh MT forging / 52,000 MT machining
•₹650 cr ultra-heavy component facility (with 20 MW captive solar) on track for Q4 FY28 commissioning; solar to add ~1.5% to EBITDA

Outlook
•Full-year volume growth guidance intact; healthy order book and ramp-up of new business provide confidence
•Gross margin and EBITDA/kg expected to trend upward on favourable mix, higher value addition and operational efficiency; full-year margins broadly similar to FY26
•Raw-material prices are pass-through; absolute EBITDA/kg has improved despite cost pressures
•New heavy-capacity and machining investments positioned for data-centre power, gas engines, wind and export CV/PV opportunities; early FY28 order conversion expected from ongoing OEM discussions
•Strong balance sheet supports further growth with limited leverage
•Overall, strong H1 delivery with profitability growing ahead of revenue; substantial CapEx pipeline (ultra-heavy + new ₹500 cr) and secured multi-year data-centre orders underpin multi-year volume and value-addition growth visibility.

CIL’s Listing-Bound Subsidiaries Log Fall in E-Auction Premiums: MCL’s Average Premium Drops Nearly 66% to ₹274 Per Tonne in FY26 From ₹802 in FY24; Incremental Revenue Falls 60% to ₹728 Crore

Core Theme 
MCL and SECL are heading toward listing with sharply lower e-auction premiums, as MCL’s much larger offering of coal in auctions found far fewer takers, cutting premiums by about two-thirds and incremental revenue by 60%, a trend that weakens a key source of higher realisation ahead of their stock market debut.

The Core Finding: Premiums Collapse
The average e-auction premium realised by Coal India’s two major subsidiaries, Mahanadi Coalfields (MCL) and South Eastern Coalfields (SECL), proposed for stock market listing, has declined by as much as two-thirds over the past two financial years

MCL and SECL are the largest and second-largest subsidiaries of Coal India in terms of coal production

According to MCL’s draft red herring prospectus (DRHP), its average premium over the notified price fell to ₹274 per tonne in FY26 from ₹802 per tonne in FY24, a decline of nearly 66%

Incremental revenue generated through premiums over notified prices also fell 60% to ₹728 crore in FY26 from ₹1,833 crore in FY24

How Coal Is Sold: FSAs vs E-Auctions
MCL and SECL sell coal mainly through two routes: Fuel supply agreements (FSAs) signed with consumers and competitive e-auction windows

Under FSAs, prices are set by Coal India and provide a stable revenue stream to the company

In e-auctions, prices are determined by demand-supply dynamics, and consumers pay premiums over and above notified prices or the benchmark prices at which bidding starts

Companies selling coal through e-auctions earn incremental revenue or “higher realisation” in the form of premiums paid by buyers

MCL: Offered vs Booked Volumes
The decline in premiums came despite a substantial increase in the quantity of coal offered through e-auctions

MCL offered 72.26 million tonnes (mt) in FY26, compared with 28.65 mt in FY24

The quantity booked rose only to 26.49 mt from 22.86 mt over the same period

Consequently, the proportion of coal offered that was booked declined from nearly 80% in FY24 to around 37% in FY26

"Guaranteed allotment" in an IPO? There is literally no such thing under SEBI ICDR regulations! 😂
  
​Holding 1 share of Coal India only qualifies you to apply under the Shareholder Quota (up to 10% reservation) for subsidiaries like SECL or MCL—it does NOT guarantee allotment. If the shareholder category gets oversubscribed (like BCCL was), it goes straight to a computerized lottery draw!
​Good strategy to get a second bidding basket alongside retail, but let's not mislabel a lottery ticket as "guaranteed free money"! 🎯📉

- Expansion of product offerings in animal nutrition and crop care, including new herbicides and value-added products.
- Strategic initiatives in the oil palm segment, including commissioning of a CPKO refinery for specialty fats.
- Anticipated inflationary trends to persist, impacting margins in the near term.

📊 GODREJ AGROVET LTD - 540743 | 🪒 Press Release / Media Release

Godrej Agrovet Ltd reports strong Q2 FY27 financial performance with a 17% revenue increase to ₹2,995 Cr, driven by growth in animal nutrition, oil palm, and B2C foods. This growth is significant as it reflects resilience amid challenging operating conditions, highlighting the company's ability to manage input cost inflation while maintaining profitability.

Company Snapshot: 
Godrej Agrovet Ltd operates in the agribusiness sector, focusing on animal nutrition, crop care, and food products. The company reported TTM Revenue of ₹11,844 Cr.

Key Highlights:
Revenue Growth 
- Q2 FY27 revenue increased by 17% YoY to ₹2,995 Cr. 
- H1 FY27 revenue grew by 13% YoY to ₹5,847 Cr. 

Profitability 
- PBT rose by 5% YoY to ₹131 Cr in Q2 FY27. 
- Profit After Tax (PAT) increased by 22% YoY to ₹103 Cr in Q2 FY27. 

Segment Performance 
- Animal nutrition revenue grew by 14% in Q2 FY27, with cattle feed volume up ~8% and layer feed up ~15%. 
- Oil palm revenue surged by 28% in Q2 FY27, driven by higher CPO (+23%) and PKO (+20%) realizations. 
- Crop care revenue rose by 42% YoY, although profitability was impacted by poor demand. 

International Growth 
- ACI-GAVL, the Bangladesh joint venture, reported a 32% revenue increase, supported by a 21% rise in volumes across poultry, cattle, and aqua segments. 

Core Growth Triggers: 
- Plantation Expansion 
- Investing in plantation expansion and commissioning of the Khammam complex, CPKO refinery, and biogas plant. 
- Expected to enhance oil palm revenue through increased production capacity. 

- Premiumization Strategy 
- Exiting the shrimp segment to focus on more profitable and scalable segments in animal nutrition. 
- Aimed at improving margins and market positioning. 

What's Already in the Price: 
The reported revenue growth and profitability metrics align with market expectations, indicating that while the results are strong, they reflect ongoing trends rather than unexpected developments.

Key Risks to Trigger Thesis: 
- Input Cost Inflation 
- Continued inflation may pressure margins, as seen with flat EBITDA despite revenue growth. 
- Crop Care Demand 
- Poor demand for cotton herbicides could further impact profitability in the crop care segment.

Godrej Agrovet | Q2 FY27 results

Godrej Agrovet Q2 profit rises 21.9% to ₹102.8 Cr, helped by other income

👉 Godrej Agrovet reported consolidated revenue of ₹2,995 Cr for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, up 16.7% from ₹2,567 Cr a year earlier and 4.9% above the June quarter's ₹2,855 Cr. Net profit was ₹102.8 Cr, up 21.9% YoY from ₹84.3 Cr but down 19.9% from ₹128.3 Cr in Q1 FY27. The unaudited results were approved by the board on November 6, 2026, with an unmodified limited review opinion.

👉 Operating profit fell faster than revenue grew. Profit before other income was ₹121.4 Cr, down 4.6% from ₹127.3 Cr, and the operating margin slipped to 4.7% from 5.2% a year earlier and 6.3% in Q1. Other income rose 179.5% to ₹21.8 Cr from ₹7.8 Cr, and that gain lifted pre-tax profit 6.0% to ₹143.2 Cr.

👉 Net profit grew faster than pre-tax profit because tax expense fell. Total tax was ₹40.5 Cr against ₹50.7 Cr in Q2 FY26, made up of current tax of ₹42.1 Cr and a deferred tax credit of ₹1.6 Cr. Profit attributable to owners of the company was ₹115.2 Cr, while the non-controlling interest recorded a loss of ₹12.5 Cr.

👉 Pre-tax growth of 6.0% falls short of the mid-teens PBT growth management guided on the August 5 call. On the August 6 call, management linked weaker crop protection volumes to a dry June that delayed Kharif sowing, and it targeted double-digit revenue growth for FY27. Revenue growth of 16.7% in Q2 sits within that target.

👉 Growth catalyst: Management guided annual capex of ₹300–350 Cr and aims to double its oil palm area to 150,000 hectares, building on the ₹300 Cr Khammam Integrated Oil Palm Complex.

👉 Road blocker: Management pointed to a dry June that delayed Kharif sowing and hurt domestic crop protection volumes, and the Q2 operating margin fell to 4.7%.

Revenue rose 16.65% to ₹2,994.98 Cr but Crop Care & Dairy posted PBIT losses

👉 Higher raw material costs eroded operating profits this quarter: combined material expenses rose to 77.28% of revenue from 73.38% a year ago, pulling EBITDA down to ₹199.73 Cr from ₹213.40 Cr despite revenue expanding to ₹2,994.98 Cr.

👉 The open question is whether high milk procurement costs and agrochemical pricing pressures begin to cool over the next two quarters, allowing Dairy and Crop Care to return to positive territory.

👉 Cash generation took a hit in the first half, with operating cash flow turning negative to an outflow of ₹142.20 Cr as inventories rose to ₹1,825.62 Cr, funded partly by stretching trade payables to ₹1,679.01 Cr.

👉 The result looks neutral because OPM of 6.67% is down from 8.41% last quarter and remains below 8.31% a year ago, as operating profit contracted 6.41% YoY.

👉 Growth catalyst: The specialty fats refinery targeted to start in late Q2/early Q3 FY27 is expected to add 200 bps to margins once fully scaled

👉 Road blocker: Firm milk procurement costs pressured Dairy into a ₹3.87 Cr PBIT loss, with elevated input prices expected to remain firm for at least two quarters

Blockers

The 9:15 | 6 November 2026

Morning. The AI trade broke overnight and India opens into the wreckage. GIFT Nifty is quoted around 24,420, down about 167 points, and that is the politest number on any screen today.

The S&P 500 fell 4.4% to 7,353.73, its worst session since April 2025. The Dow dropped 1,833 points. The Nasdaq lost 5.5% and is now roughly 12% below its record close a month ago. The Philadelphia Semiconductor index fell 12.2% in one session. Asia followed hard: Kospi down 8.7% to 4,911 and a circuit breaker tripped, Nikkei down as much as 7%, SK Hynix off 11.7%, Samsung nearly 10%, TSMC 8.5%, SoftBank 11%. Shanghai was off only 1.1% and Hang Seng 0.6%, so this is a memory-and-semis event rather than a general Asia event.

The explanation on offer is the US midterms: Democrats took Congress on 3 November and the market has decided that means tighter AI scrutiny and a slower data-centre build-out. I would hold that loosely. A 12% semiconductor day usually has more positioning in it than politics. US futures were green in the Asian session and the US 10-year is at 4.838%, near its lowest since 9 September.

Now the part that matters more for India than the Nasdaq does. Crude has snapped back. Brent January is around $99.86, up 1.6%, a second straight gain, with WTI at $91.62. Iran said three more tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, and ANZ reckons flows through the strait are under 60% of capacity. The best macro gift India had this week, Brent settling at a two-month low after an 8% collapse on Wednesday, has been handed back in two sessions. Brent is still down about 12% on the week, but a market that spent Thursday buying paints, airlines and OMCs on $94 crude now has to look at $100 again.

Gold and silver futures are softer, down about 0.93% and 1%, with spot gold near $4,086. Awkward timing, because today is Dhanteras.

Domestically, the new thing is Coal India: subsidiary Mahanadi Coalfields has SEBI clearance for an IPO that is entirely an offer-for-sale of up to 66.18 crore shares. MCL was 28% of Coal India's FY26 coal production, so this is a value-unlock question for the parent, not a listing-day story. ONGC printed standalone PAT of Rs 15,488.6cr, up 57.3%, plus a record Rs 8 interim dividend, all earned on crude that no longer exists at that level. Prestige Estates profit fell 44%.

Three things to watch. Whether the foreign bid holds: FIIs net bought Rs 14,975cr on Thursday, the biggest day of a five-session run, with DIIs selling Rs 10,445cr into it, and a global risk event is the cleanest test that run has faced. Crude at $100 and what it does to the pass-through trade. And IT at the open, with Infosys and TCS the local proxy for a 12% SOX day.

More after the close.

Elon Daily 20261105

① Tesla and SpaceX Plunge as Market Values Shrink

November 5 closing prices:

🔴 TSLA: $343.69 (-10.77%), intraday low $338.15.

🔴 SPCX: $123.39 (-9.22%), intraday low $120.39.

Both fell for a second consecutive day. Reuters reported that their combined market value losses this week were estimated to have exceeded $380 billion at one point.

Three major concerns:

• Potential regulatory changes following Democrats’ midterm victories.

• Political uncertainty surrounding Texas AI data centers and the proposed Terafab project.

• Increased scrutiny of a potential Tesla–SpaceX merger.

But the Nasdaq also fell roughly 5.5%. Politics alone cannot explain the selloff.

My take: Investors are reassessing the returns on massive AI capital spending. For Tesla and SpaceX, delivering cash flow matters more than ambitious growth narratives.

② Goldman Sachs Flags Risks to 45% of Planned U.S. Data Center Expansion

Goldman Sachs warns that Democratic victories could encourage additional states to impose temporary moratoriums on new data centers.

Under this scenario, roughly 45% of planned U.S. capacity expansion could face disruption.

For SpaceX’s AI business, the challenge goes beyond GPU prices. Power availability, permits, and deployment timelines determine when computing assets can generate revenue.

Important: 45% represents potential exposure, not confirmed project cancellations.

③ FAA Proposes Major Space Launch Regulatory Reform

On November 5, the FAA proposed simplifying commercial launch and reentry regulations.

The changes address flight-abort requirements, debris-risk assessments, and licensing procedures.

The agency also plans broader licensing reforms in 2027, supporting a national goal of at least 1,000 annual launches and reentries by 2030.

For SpaceX, faster approvals could enable more frequent Starship launches.

The proposed rules are not yet fully in effect.

④ Robotaxi Industry Faces New State-Level Regulatory Uncertainty

The midterm elections have changed the political landscape in several key states.

Tesla’s Cybercab and Waymo’s expansion plans could face changes in autonomous-vehicle safety regulations.

But election results do not automatically mean driverless operations will be restricted.

The key questions: Will incoming state governments change operating permits, safety reporting requirements, or deployment rules?

⑤ Waymo and Lyft Expand Nashville Robotaxi Operations

Lyft plans to expand its Waymo fleet operations in Nashville and develop airport service.

Lyft handles vehicle maintenance, charging, cleaning, and other fleet operations.

An important lesson for Tesla:

Robotaxi competition isn’t just about FSD algorithms. It’s also about fleet utilization, operating costs, charging efficiency, and customer experience.

Ultimately, the companies that deliver reliable autonomous rides at sustainable costs will have the strongest business models.

Elon系日报 20261105

① Tesla、SpaceX双双暴跌，市值大幅缩水

11月5日美股收盘：

🔴 TSLA：$343.69，跌10.77%，盘中最低$338.15。

🔴 SPCX：$123.39，跌9.22%，盘中最低$120.39。

两家公司连续第二天下跌。Reuters报道，本周两家公司合计市值损失一度预计超过3,800亿美元。

市场担忧三大风险：

• 民主党中期选举获胜后，监管环境可能改变。

• 德州AI数据中心及Terafab项目面临政策不确定性。

• Tesla–SpaceX潜在合并可能遭遇更严格审查。

但纳斯达克当天也下跌约5.5%，不能将全部跌幅归因于政治。

我的判断：市场正在重新评估AI巨额资本开支的回报。对Tesla和SpaceX而言，现金流兑现能力比增长故事更重要。

② 高盛警告：美国45%的规划数据中心扩张可能受到影响

Goldman Sachs分析认为，民主党选举胜利可能推动更多州暂停批准新数据中心。

潜在受影响容量约占美国规划扩张的45%。

对SpaceX旗下AI业务而言，风险不仅是GPU价格，还有电力供应、建设许可及设备投产时间。

注意：45%是风险情景，不是已经停建的比例。

③ FAA提出商业航天监管改革，SpaceX有望受益

11月5日，美国FAA提出简化商业火箭发射和再入审批的规则。

改革涉及飞行中止条件、碎片风险评估及许可程序。

FAA还计划2027年全面改革发射许可制度，以支持2030年每年至少1,000次发射和再入的目标。

对SpaceX而言，审批效率提升可能支持Starship更高频率发射。但新规则尚未全部生效。

④ Robotaxi面临新的州级监管不确定性

美国中期选举改变了部分关键州的政治格局。

Tesla Cybercab与Waymo未来的商业扩张，都可能受到自动驾驶安全监管政策变化的影响。

不过，选举结果不等于无人驾驶禁令。

真正需要关注的是：新一届州政府是否修改无人驾驶许可、安全报告和运营要求。

⑤ Waymo与Lyft扩大Nashville Robotaxi运营

Lyft计划扩大其支持运营的Waymo无人驾驶车队，并推进机场服务。

Lyft负责车辆维护、充电、清洁等运营环节。

这对Tesla是一个提醒：

Robotaxi竞争不仅是FSD算法，还有车队利用率、运营成本、充电效率和用户体验。

未来谁能以更低成本提供可靠的无人驾驶出行服务，谁才更有机会建立可持续的商业模式。

Sansera Engineering reported a record Q2 FY27, with revenue of ₹10,915 Mn, up 32% YoY, and PAT of ₹1,086 Mn, up 52%. EBITDA grew 48% to a 19.4% margin, against 17.3% a year earlier. The Nichidai JV's commercial production has slipped to H2 FY27 from a Q3 start. Management flagged inflationary input costs, geopolitical uncertainty and wage pressures.

Growth triggers
• FY27 ADS revenue guidance of ₹5,500–6,000 Mn.
• Planned FY27 capex of about ₹8,000 Mn.
• Nichidai JV commercial production expected in H2 FY27.

Blockers
• Inflationary input costs, geopolitical uncertainty and wage cost pressures.
• Nichidai JV timeline softened: on stream from Q3 FY27 is now expected in H2 FY27.

Sanjivani Paranteral | Q2 FY27 results

Sanjivani Paranteral's Q2 profit rises 156% to ₹4.1 Cr on 63% revenue growth

👉 Sanjivani Paranteral reported consolidated revenue from operations of ₹25.3 Cr for Q2 FY27, up 63.2% from ₹15.5 Cr a year earlier and 6.3% from Q1. Net profit rose to ₹4.1 Cr from ₹1.6 Cr, a 156.2% gain, and 64% above the ₹2.5 Cr posted in Q1. Profit before tax was ₹5.5 Cr. Other income was only ₹0.1 Cr, so the gain came from core operations.

👉 Operating margin rose to 21.7% from 14.0% a year earlier and 13.7% in Q1. Material costs were ₹12.1 Cr, against ₹10.7 Cr a year ago, while employee costs rose to ₹2.5 Cr from ₹1.5 Cr. Depreciation climbed to ₹0.7 Cr from ₹0.2 Cr as the Pune plant ramped up.

👉 Half-year operating cash flow was ₹1.3 Cr, against ₹0.1 Cr a year ago, after tax payments of ₹0.8 Cr. Trade receivables rose to ₹17.0 Cr from ₹15.4 Cr at March 31, and other current assets rose to ₹9.5 Cr from ₹5.1 Cr. Total borrowings stood at about ₹16.4 Cr, up from ₹14.3 Cr. Capex in the half was ₹1.7 Cr, down from ₹6.0 Cr a year earlier.

👉 Half-year revenue of ₹49.2 Cr is about a third of the ₹140-150 Cr FY27 guidance management gave in August, which combines ₹80-85 Cr from the base business and ₹60-65 Cr from the Pune IV-fluid plant. Finance costs rose to ₹0.4 Cr from ₹0.05 Cr. The filing's split of profit between owners and non-controlling interest does not add up to the total, so this report uses the net profit line.

👉 Growth catalyst: Management's FY27 guidance of ₹60-65 Cr from the Pune IV-fluid plant, with a 17-18% EBITDA margin target for the IVF business, is the next test.

👉 Road blocker: Half-year operating cash flow of ₹1.3 Cr is small against ₹6.6 Cr of net profit, as receivables rose ₹1.6 Cr.

Revenue rose 32.27% to ₹1,091.45 Cr, but debt doubled to ₹636.32 Cr

👉 Revenue rose to ₹1,091.45 Cr from ₹825.20 Cr a year ago as aerospace dispatches and core machining demand expanded.

👉 Core profit followed, with EBITDA rising to ₹211.23 Cr and OPM expanding to 19.35%. Combined material costs dropped to 38.17% of revenue from 41.53% last year, though an inventory build provided much of that cost relief.

NCL organised a one-day training programme on “Leadership Excellence, Conflict Management, Driving Organisational Change, Personal Branding & Executive Presence” as part of capacity building training program under Vigilance Awareness Campaign Marathon Training Program 3.0 Mission-CIL@2026 at MDI, Singrauli on Wednesday.

During the session, Shri Krishna Mohan, Retired IAS Officer (1977 Batch), Haryana Cadre shared insights including importance of effective communication, strategic thinking, adaptability, interpersonal skills and a positive leadership approach in achieving organisational goals.

The programme aimed at strengthening the leadership and managerial competencies of NCL executives by providing insights into effective leadership practices, conflict resolution, change management and professional development. The session also focused on developing leadership excellence, managing workplace conflicts constructively, driving organisational transformation and building a strong professional identity through personal branding and executive presence.

Around 42 participants from all NCL Areas & Units attended the programme.

What makes "Samhi Hotels" a serious investment case?

👉For context: FY26 revenue was rupees 1248 Crore.

Samhi Hotels (SAMHI) has a secured development pipeline of roughly 1,669-1,700 rooms (on top of ~4,899 operational rooms as of FY26), which is expected to expand the portfolio toward ~6,500–6,600 rooms by FY31.

👉This pipeline, focused heavily on the upscale/upper-upscale segment, is a core driver of management’s outlook for revenue potential rising from ~₹1,280 crore in FY26 toward ~₹2,300 crore from new inventory alone, and ~₹3,000 crore overall over the next four years when combined with same-store growth.

➡️ Breakdown of pipeline

~1,669–1,700 new rooms across ~7 major hotels/projects, with the majority in upscale/upper-upscale.

👉✅️This is expected to lift the share of upscale inventory from ~41% to ~60% by FY2030.

▶️Notable projects:

1. W Hotel, HITEC City, Hyderabad (~170 rooms, upper upscale): Targeted to open around Q2 FY28 (stabilized year FY29); conversion of an existing office building under a long-term variable lease.

2. Westin + Tribute Portfolio, Whitefield, Bengaluru: Dual-branded expansion/rebranding (opening targeted around FY29-FY30).

3. Navi Mumbai dual-branded project (~700 rooms total under Westin upper-upscale and Fairfield by Marriott upper mid-scale, in phases starting with ~400): 👉Largest project by room count; near Navi Mumbai International Airport and DY Patil Stadium.

Construction progressing after MIDC timeline extension; major contribution expected later in the pipeline (around FY31).

4. Noida (~162-room upper-upscale hotel) with Ingka Centres (IKEA Group affiliate): capital-efficient variable lease model (Ingka builds structure; Samhi handles fit-outs); opening targeted FY30.

5. Marriott-branded hotel in Sriperumbudur/Chennai area (~135 rooms), 
additional Hyderabad Financial District mid-scale (~260 rooms under variable lease), 
expansions/rebrandings (including ~473 rooms being converted/upgraded).

👉Limited contribution in the near term (e.g., some openings/impact from FY27-FY28 onward), ramping meaningfully from FY28/FY29 with larger additions in later years (including the bulk of Navi Mumbai).

👉Capex for the pipeline is estimated around ₹2,200 crore, to be funded largely from internal free cash flows.​

➡️ How the pipeline augments growth
Revenue expansion: 

👉Pipeline alone is expected to add ~₹1,000 crore to annual revenue.

👉Combined with same-store growth guidance of 9-11% annually (recently running stronger, e.g., 12.6% same-store revenue and 14.3% RevPAR growth in Q2 FY27), this supports overall revenue opportunity of ~₹3,000 crore over ~4 years & path toward high-teens (or potentially early-20s) revenue growth once new inventory ramps. 

👉New hotels begin contributing more visibly from FY28.​

➡️ Mix shift and margins: 

Higher-ADR upscale inventory drives revenue per key and supports operating EBITDA margins moving toward ~40% as the mix improves.

➡️ Cash flow and balance sheet strength: 

👉Management targets >₹3,000 crore cumulative free cash flow over FY27-FY31. 

This is intended to fund the pipeline with limited additional debt.

Recent GIC partnership (35% stake in an upscale platform) has already helped cut debt and lower interest costs.

➡️ Complementary asset-light growth: 

The RARE India platform (~70-75 hotels / ~1,000+ rooms in experiential/leisure) adds high-margin fee income (meaningful contribution expected from FY28 onward, with Marriott distribution partnership enhancing reach). This diversifies into leisure without heavy capital intensity.

Overall, the pipeline provides visible, multi-year visibility on room additions concentrated in high-demand commercial corridors (Hyderabad, Bengaluru, NCR, Mumbai region, Chennai).

SAMHI Hotels: Q2 FY27 Results and Key Takeaways from the Concall

Same-store growth beat the long-term guidance again. The GST drag on margins ends from next quarter, and the W Hyderabad opening is now close.

Q2 FY27 Numbers
Total income: ₹342.7 Cr (+15.6% YoY)
EBITDA: ₹123.8 Cr (+12% YoY), margin 36.1%
EBITDA excluding GST impact: ₹133.8 Cr (+21.3% YoY), margin 39.1%
Profit before tax and one-offs: ₹53.4 Cr (+39.9% YoY)
PAT: ₹41.1 Cr (last year's base had ₹84.1 Cr of one-time gains)
Occupancy: 78.6% (vs 75%) | Same-store RevPAR: +14%

H1 FY27 Numbers
Profit before tax and one-offs: ₹86.2 Cr (+35.4% YoY)
PAT: ₹66 Cr

1.  Hotels are filling up and gaining pricing power-
RevPAR (Revenue Per Available Room) is room revenue divided by all rooms, so it rises when either room rates or occupancy go up. On 37% of nights the hotels were above 90% full, up from 32% a year ago, and full nights allow higher pricing. About 80% of guests were domestic. Bangalore and Hyderabad together absorbed 7.9 million sq ft of new office space this quarter, which feeds hotel demand. Hyderabad RevPAR grew 19.1%, Pune 17.2% and Bangalore 8% on a high base.

2.  GST drag ends from next quarter-
Changes in GST rules took away input tax credit, costing about ₹10 Cr a quarter. Last year's base absorbs this impact from Q3, so management expects reported EBITDA growth in the high teens from here. The GST Council has suggested limited relief for hotels charging below ₹7,500 a night, but the final notification is awaited.

3.  Moving upmarket with W Hyderabad-
The 170-room W hotel in Hyderabad's Hitec City should be built by the end of FY27. Opening is planned for Q2 FY28, with a buffer for fire and other approvals. Once it stabilises in FY29, it could add over 10% to the FY27 revenue base. Upscale hotels earned EBITDA margins about 800 bps higher than the rest of the portfolio in the last six months. Their share of income should rise from 42% to about 60% by FY30.

4.  New hotels funded from internal cash-
The secured pipeline adds about 1,670 rooms and upgrades 473 more. Key projects are the Westin and Tribute in Bangalore (370 rooms), a 162-room hotel in Noida, a 134-room Marriott in Sriperumbudur and 658 rooms in Navi Mumbai. Capex of about ₹2,250 Cr over FY27-31 is planned from internal cash, with net debt staying around current levels.

5.  RARE India, a low-capital fee business-
RARE India's boutique hotels go live on Marriott Bonvoy's Outdoor Collection in December, and SAMHI earns about an 18% commission on bookings. Management expects ₹15-20 Cr of revenue from this in FY28 with almost no capex. The platform has about 70 hotels now and should reach 85-90.

6.  Debt steady, more profit to come-
Net debt is ₹1,458 Cr, or 3.1 times trailing EBITDA (2.2 times after adjusting for money tied up in hotels under construction). Two small hotels worth ₹200-230 Cr may be sold to recycle capital. About ₹100 Cr of deferred tax asset is expected to be recognised in Q4. This is a book entry for past losses that can now be set off against future taxable profit, and it will boost reported PAT.

Key Guidance
Same-store revenue growth of 9-11% over the long term
RevPAR growth of about 14-15% in H2
Net debt to EBITDA of 2.5 times in about 18 months

https://t.co/Jf0ZTYDxbx

*Valuation & View:* We initiate coverage on Sammaan Capital with a BUY rating and a target price of INR 360. Sammaan is a mortgage-led NBFC in the RBI's upper layer, now controlled by Abu Dhabi's IHC, that is turning multi-product after a completed balance-sheet clean-up. The FY26 reset took GNPA and NNPA to nil, and IHC's backing has already lifted the company to AA+ at all three domestic rating agencies. We expect RoE to build from 7.5% in FY27E to about 16% by FY30E. The drivers are a falling cost of funds as the liability side re-rates, monetisation of the legacy pool, new high-yield products (gold, personal loans, micro-LAP) and operating leverage from the branch build-out. We expect PAT to compound at about 44% over FY27E to FY30E. At a CMP of INR 120, the stock trades at about 0.67x FY29E ABV of INR 179 and 14% below IHC's INR 139 entry price, a level we believe gives little credit to the recovery already underway. *We value Sammaan at 2.0x FY29E ABV, a plan-delivery multiple with a 24 to 30 month horizon, to arrive at a target price of INR 360, implying upside of about 200% (12-month discounted value INR 296).*

OnEMI Technology Solutions Ltd (Kissht) delivered a robust performance in Q2 FY27, marked by significant growth in Assets Under Management (AUM) and Profit After Tax (PAT), alongside strategic shifts towards higher-quality customers and improved operational efficiencies.

𝗙𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝗛𝗶𝗴𝗵𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝘀:

- 𝗣𝗔𝗧 𝗗𝗼𝘂𝗯𝗹𝗲𝘀 𝗬𝗼𝗬: Profit After Tax surged to ₹125 Cr, a 100% increase compared to the previous year, and up 31.6% QoQ.
- 𝗔𝗨𝗠 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘁𝗵: AUM reached ₹9,317 Cr, demonstrating a strong YoY growth of 68.4% and 16.4% QoQ.
- 𝗖𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗿 𝗕𝗮𝘀𝗲 𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻: Served 12.8 million customers (up 22.5% YoY), with active customers growing 58% YoY to 3.61 million.
- 𝗥𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗻𝘂𝗲 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘁𝗵: Total income stood at ₹740 Cr, up 43% YoY.
- 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗳𝗶𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗠𝗲𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗰𝘀: Return on average AUM improved to 5.78%, and Return on Average Equity was 21.65%.

𝗦𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗴𝗶𝗰 𝗙𝗼𝗰𝘂𝘀 & 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗘𝗳𝗳𝗶𝗰𝗶𝗲𝗻𝗰𝘆:

- 𝗦𝗵𝗶𝗳𝘁 𝘁𝗼 𝗤𝘂𝗮𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗖𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗿𝘀: The company is deliberately focusing on less leveraged customers with higher credit scores, leading to increased average ticket size (now ₹43,380) and longer average tenure (17.8 months).
- 𝗖𝗼𝘀𝘁 𝗼𝗳 𝗕𝗼𝗿𝗿𝗼𝘄𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗥𝗲𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: The average cost of borrowing decreased by approximately 70 basis points to 13.76%, with further reductions expected due to improved credit ratings.
- 𝗧𝗲𝗰𝗵𝗻𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝘆 𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗴𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: AI and machine learning are core to operations, enhancing underwriting (AUC improved to 75%), fraud detection, and collections (voice agents recovering 85% of human caller rates).
- 𝗟𝗔𝗣 𝗕𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘀 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗳𝗶𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆: The Loan Against Property (LAP) business turned profitable in Q2 FY27, ahead of guidance.

𝗔𝘀𝘀𝗲𝘁 𝗤𝘂𝗮𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗜𝗺𝗽𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁:

- 𝗥𝗲𝗱𝘂𝗰𝗲𝗱 𝗖𝗿𝗲𝗱𝗶𝘁 𝗖𝗼𝘀𝘁𝘀: Credit costs fell to 6.2% of average AUM from 9.3% a year ago.
- 𝗟𝗼𝘄𝗲𝗿 𝗡𝗣𝗔𝘀: Gross NPA improved to 2.18%, and Net NPA stood at 0.34%.
- 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗴𝗲-2 & 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗴𝗲-3: Stage-2 assets reduced to 2.37%, and Stage-3 coverage remains strong at 84.6%.

𝗙𝘂𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗚𝘂𝗶𝗱𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲:

SAMHI Hotels concall. One simple sum explains the whole story.

For two years, 98% of SAMHI’s revenue has been same-store. No new hotel opened. The company grew 12 to 15% a quarter purely by filling the same rooms at higher rates. Management guides 9 to 11% for that engine and has delivered 10.4% over three years.

Now layer the next bit. W Hyderabad opens in Q2 FY28. At full capacity it should do about ₹170 cr a year, roughly 6 to 7% on top of SAMHI’s revenue base by then.

So the old hotels give you 10%. The new one gives you another 6 to 7%. Put together, SAMHI goes from a 10% growth company to a 16 to 17% one, before RARE adds its first ₹15 to 20 cr of fee income 📈

Then a new hotel every six quarters or so till FY31. Sheraton Hyderabad rooms, Westin Bangalore, the IKEA Noida hotel, Sriperumbudur, Navi Mumbai. The CEO’s words: back to high teens, if not early 20s, which is what this company compounded at from FY12 to FY26.

And the part I care about most as a shareholder: net debt stays at ₹1,450 to 1,500 cr through all of it. ₹2,250 cr of capex funded from cash. Below 3x by March, 2.5x in 18 months. No equity, no stress 🏦

The GST adjustment that has muddied every print for four quarters drops out from Q3. Reported EBITDA growth goes back to high teens on its own.

Execution is the risk, not demand. Fire approvals on W have a cushion built in. Navi Mumbai is a FY31 story. But the growth that was a promise at IPO now has dates on it.

Stay not out

Samhi Hotels | Q2 FY27 results

Samhi net profit falls 58.8% to ₹41.1 Cr on last year's ₹84 Cr one-off

👉 Samhi Hotels reported consolidated net profit of ₹41.1 Cr for Q2 FY27, down 58.8% from ₹99.8 Cr a year earlier. The comparison is distorted by base effects: Q2 FY26 carried ₹84.1 Cr of exceptional income, against ₹3.9 Cr this quarter. Profit attributable to owners of the company was ₹33.5 Cr, against ₹92.4 Cr a year ago.

👉 Revenue from operations rose 15.4% YoY to ₹338.1 Cr and 10.8% QoQ from ₹305.2 Cr. Other income rose 35.3% to ₹4.6 Cr. Profit before exceptional items and tax was ₹53.4 Cr, against ₹38.2 Cr in Q2 FY26. Tax expense was ₹16.2 Cr, against ₹19.9 Cr a year ago.

👉 OPM was 16.7%, down 2,456 bps from 41.3% a year earlier but up 611 bps from 10.6% in Q1 FY27. Profit excluding other income rose 40.2% to ₹48.8 Cr. Management had flagged mid-scale margin pressure from GST changes on the Q1 call, and said it was pivoting toward upscale assets.

👉 Six-month revenue rose 13.8% to ₹643.3 Cr from ₹565.2 Cr, and operating cash flow was ₹225.8 Cr against ₹165.6 Cr. Capital expenditure was ₹134.7 Cr. Cash and cash equivalents fell to ₹93.8 Cr at 30 September from ₹158.8 Cr at 31 March, while total borrowings rose to ₹1,730 Cr from ₹1,708 Cr.

👉 Growth catalyst: Management plans to open the W Hyderabad hotel in Q4 FY27 within a pipeline of seven hotels and 1,669 rooms, as stated on the Q1 FY27 earnings call.

👉 Road blocker: Management named mid-scale margin compression from GST changes, and reported OPM of 16.7% was down 2,456 bps year on year.

SAMHI Hotels Q2 FY27. PAT down 59%. Don’t fall for it.

Last year’s Q2 had ₹841 mn of one-offs (land impairment reversal + Caspia Delhi sale gain). This year has ₹39 mn. Strip both and PAT ex-exceptional is ₹372 mn, up 137%. PBT before exceptional ₹534 mn, up 40% on 16% revenue growth. Those are the numbers that matter 📊

Underneath: same-store occupancy 78.6% (vs 75%), RevPAR +14.3%, ARR +9.2%. One in three days was sold out. All this while air traffic in its core cities fell 11-13% and international demand stayed weak. Domestic business travel is carrying the load.

The GST change (12% with ITC to 5% without) shaved ₹103 mn off EBITDA. Ex that, EBITDA grew 21% at a 39% margin. One-time reset in the base, fades as the mix shifts upscale.

Finance cost down 10% YoY, interest rate 7.8% vs 10.8% at IPO. Net debt ₹14.6 bn, up just ₹72 mn since March despite capex on three hotels.

Growth has been same-store only for 6 quarters. That ends Q2 FY28 with W Hyderabad, then 1,669 rooms secured through FY31. Plus RARE India goes live on Marriott Bonvoy in December 🏨

Advait Energy Transitions: Q2 FY27 Results and Key Takeaways from the Concall

Advait provides power transmission products and is expanding into battery storage and green hydrogen. Profit grew 89% and its order book is up 47%.

Q2 FY27 (consolidated)
Revenue: ₹221 Cr (+40.8% YoY)
EBITDA: ₹32 Cr (+84.4% YoY), margin 14.5% (vs 11%)
PAT: ₹19 Cr (+88.5% YoY), margin 8.7%
H1 FY27 revenue: ₹400 Cr (+45.4% YoY)
H1 FY27 PAT: ₹34 Cr (+77.9% YoY)
Order book (including L1): about ₹1,575 Cr (+47% YoY)

1.  Order book growing fast-
The order book, including projects where Advait is the lowest bidder, grew 47% to about ₹1,575 Cr. It completed orders worth about ₹400 Cr in H1. This gives healthy revenue visibility.

2.  Transmission business steady-
Advait won distribution orders from Gujarat power utilities, including about ₹52 Cr from DGVCL. It also won orders for emergency restoration systems, OPGW (power lines with built-in optical fibre) and stringing tools. India's continued investment in transmission supports demand.

3.  Battery storage push-
Advait won a 150 MW / 300 MWh standalone battery storage project in Junagadh. A 2.5 GWh battery manufacturing plant, expandable to 5 GWh, should start by Q4 FY27. Machinery orders have already been placed.

4.  Green hydrogen progress-
Advait's electrolyser technology, which splits water into hydrogen, is being tested in a 5 MW program. It is engaging with over 13 Indian green hydrogen players. It has also signed an offtake agreement with battery maker Hithium for its upcoming orders.

5.  New integrated factory-
Phase 1 of the integrated manufacturing facility at Gangad, Gujarat should start by Q4 FY27. It will support transmission, substation and renewable energy products.

6.  Big long-term ambition-
Management has outlined a target of ₹5,000 Cr revenue in about 5 years, about 7 times FY26 revenue. It says this depends on investor and funding support. Margins should improve as more revenue comes from manufactured products.

Key Guidance
FY27 capex of ₹300-350 Cr
Battery plant and Gangad facility operational by Q4 FY27
Long-term target of ₹5,000 Cr revenue in about 5 years
